extracted.intended_audience: researchers, clinicians, and scientists who conduct peer review for medical/scientific journals
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for conducting ethical, professional, and high-quality peer reviews of medical/scientific manuscripts, including responsibilities, timeliness, conflicts of interest, confidentiality, tone, and content of reviews.

rubrics_metrics.name: Adhere to COPE guidelines
rubrics_metrics.description: JGIM follows the Committee on Publication Ethics (COPE) guidelines for managing manuscripts; COPE states reviewers are responsible for timeliness and professionalism and are required to declare any conflicts of interest prior to completing a review.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow COPE recommendations on reviewer responsibilities (timeliness, professionalism, conflicts). See COPE Ethical guidelines for peer reviewers (Version 2: September 2017).

rubrics_metrics.name: Timeliness
rubrics_metrics.description: Timeliness encompasses both responses to the journal on whether the reviewer is willing to conduct the peer review and, if so, conducting the review in a timely manner.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: JGIM gives reviewers 4 business days to respond to invitations and 14 days to complete the review. Respond promptly to invitations and meet the agreed deadline for submission.

rubrics_metrics.name: Review within scope of expertise
rubrics_metrics.description: Review science within your scope of expertise as a professional responsibility to ensure fidelity and growth of evidence-based research.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the manuscript lies outside your expertise, decline so the editor can find an appropriate reviewer; only accept assignments you can evaluate competently.

rubrics_metrics.name: Declare and manage conflicts of interest; recuse if necessary
rubrics_metrics.description: Before agreeing to review, the reviewer must determine if there are potential conflicts of interest. 'Competing interests may be personal, financial, intellectual, professional, political or religious in nature.' Reviewers are responsible for declaring to the editors any potential relationships or activities that might bias evaluations and to recuse themselves from the peer-review process if a conflict exists.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If unsure about a potential bias, contact the editor to make the final decision. Declare all relevant relationships/activities to editors prior to completing the review.

rubrics_metrics.name: Maintain confidentiality and respect authors' intellectual property
rubrics_metrics.description: Professionalism includes maintaining confidentiality throughout the peer review process. Reviewers must understand that the manuscript and the ideas in the manuscript are privileged and confidential information and the property of the authors.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not share manuscript details or copy any ideas or novel methods until the manuscript is published. Keep all submitted material private and secure.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use a professional, constructive tone; avoid personal agenda
rubrics_metrics.description: Professionalism also includes refraining from using an overly critical tone, being self-referential, or pushing a personal agenda in a review.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide constructive, honest, and polite comments. Avoid ad hominem language, gratuitous harshness, or using reviews to advance personal viewpoints.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provide feedback aimed at improving the work
rubrics_metrics.description: Even if you do not believe the article under review should be published, providing feedback to improve the work may benefit a resubmission in the future.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explain major concerns clearly and offer actionable suggestions where possible; focus on helping authors understand how to strengthen the manuscript.

rubrics_metrics.name: Appropriate handling of citation suggestions; avoid impact-factor manipulation
rubrics_metrics.description: Peer-reviewers and editors should refrain from unethical practices aimed to boost a journal’s impact factor, such as requesting authors to include additional citations from the journal.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: You may critique references and suggest additional references (including your own) but suggest your own publications very judiciously and only if they provide valuable additional background. Avoid systematically 'stacking' citations for impact factor.

rubrics_metrics.name: Content balance: big-picture and specific comments without excessive summary
rubrics_metrics.description: A quality review incorporates both big picture and specific comments without summarizing the article in detail. The peer reviewer’s ultimate job is to assess whether an article merits publication.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Focus comments on significance, validity, clarity, and areas needing change; avoid long verbatim summaries of the manuscript that merely repeat content for the editor/author.

rubrics_metrics.name: Thoroughness: read all submitted material carefully
rubrics_metrics.description: A thorough review requires a careful read of all submitted material; dedicating time to conducting a quality review means higher quality publications.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examine main text, figures, tables, appendices, and supplementary material as needed to assess methods, results, and conclusions fully.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of confidential comments to editors only when necessary
rubrics_metrics.description: Most reviews do not need confidential comments to the editor. Editor comments should be reserved for remarks that the author should not see only if they will help the editor make a decision.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For example, if selecting 'reject', you might clarify primary concerns in confidential comments, but do not use the section to reiterate recommendations or put comments authors should see. Editors may use discretion and add such comments to letters to authors.

rubrics_metrics.name: Pursue training and improvement in reviewing skills
rubrics_metrics.description: Most reviewers have little, if any, formal training in conducting reviews; understanding the ethics of peer review is an important component of scientific practice. Continuing to improve on peer review skills and understanding ethical components will lead to stronger science.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Seek formal resources and courses (e.g., 'Focus on Peer Review' through Nature Masterclasses) and gain experience to hone reviewing skills, even if already experienced.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid self-serving reviewer behavior (self-reference, pushing own work)
rubrics_metrics.description: Reviewers should refrain from being self-referential or pushing a personal agenda in a review; they may suggest their own publications only judiciously if relevant.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Separate legitimate scholarly suggestions (including your own work when clearly relevant) from attempts to inappropriately promote personal or professional gain.

rubrics_metrics.name: Seek editor guidance when in doubt
rubrics_metrics.description: If a reviewer is unsure about a potential bias or whether to accept a review, contacting the editor to make the final decision is best practice.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use editor judgment for borderline conflicts, scope uncertainties, or procedural questions rather than making unilateral decisions.
